subject: Discovery recap — tool calling & structured output (ACME.ai)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 15:14:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — tool calling & structured output (ACME.ai)

Hi Aditi (and team),

Thanks again for the intro call earlier — great to meet you all. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

Attendees:
- Aditi Shah (ACME)
- Rahul Mehta (ACME)
- Sara Li (ACME)
- Jordan Blake (Redwood)
- Lauren Bishop (Redwood)

Primary pain points you shared:
- Inference outputs are currently noisy for structured downstream consumers; you need deterministic JSON responses for downstream ingestion and billing pipelines.
- Tool/function calling reliability is inconsistent (missing fields, inconsistent types), causing retries and orchestration complexity.
- Latency spikes during peak micro-batch windows; current SLA needs: p95 latency < 200ms for single-turn calls.

Current stack you described:
- Frontend event collector -> in-house agent orchestrator -> hosted LLM API for generation -> post-processing to map to JSON schema.
- Some function calls are performed by the orchestrator; others are expected to be emitted by the model as structured JSON that triggers downstream services.

Success criteria (what would make this successful for ACME):
1) Deterministic, validateable JSON output (schema-driven) at >98% pass rate on your eval set.
2) Reliable tool/function calling with explicit function identifiers and typed arguments so your orchestrator can route without ad-hoc parsing.
3) Latency SLOs: p95 <200ms, error rate <1% for production traffic.
4) Clear unit economics: predictable token and call cost under projected throughput.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood: share an initial draft JSON schema and example prompts/templates (attached: example-schema.json).
- ACME: share a small set of representative sample payloads (2–3 examples) and an eval prompt that you use today.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45m) to walk engineer-to-engineer through function calling wiring and agent workflows.
- Align on a 4-week pilot scope and success metrics; I attached a short mutual-action-plan draft (mutual-action-plan.pdf).

Possible TD slots: Mon 3/22 10:00–11:00 PT, Tue 3/23 08:00–11:00 PT. Please confirm what works.

Thanks — I’ll get the draft JSON schema over by EOD today so your engineers have something to review.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Jordan — this looks right to us.

Couple quick clarifications:
- The deterministic JSON requirement is mainly for our billing and downstream analytics pipelines; schema validation failures today cause manual intervention.
- For tool calling we need explicit function IDs (not free-form labels) and strong typing on arguments (string/int/enum) so our orchestrator can map directly to RPCs.
- We can share 3 sample payloads (happy path + 2 common failure cases) by EOD tomorrow.

Rahul and Sara are looping in to help with the technical deep-dive. Tue 3/23 09:00 PT works for the engs on our side.

—Aditi
